correctness.rationale: Both finite permutations preserve principal two-sided ideal classes: iterate first the inequality for the output around its cycles, then the inequality from the input to its image around the mapping cycles. The intervening powers force s^2 J s for every s when k>=2. Independently, write s=a s^2 b in S^1; iterating s=a s(sb) and s=(as)s b with idempotent powers of a and b gives s in s^2 S^1 and in S^1 s^2. Thus every positive power is H-equivalent to s, including an idempotent power, so s lies in a group. For even k, at most two residues are excluded at odd primes and only zero at 2; an exponent coprime to the exponent of each group induces a permutation even without commutativity. For E=1 the constraints are vacuous. In a Clifford semigroup the group-index map to the semilattice identifies each principal ideal with the fibers below its index, so both permutations preserve the fibers, and disjoint union gives the converse. For odd k the kth power is invertible on abelian 2-groups; the abelian Hall–Paige criterion applies there, while the CRT argument works on odd-order factors. The unique involution obstructs the remaining case by multiplying the mapping equations. The inspected verifier uses the exact finite definition (42 advertised table/exponent combinations and a separate k=1 contrast); it was not rerun and the universal decisions do not depend on it.
residual_risks: No general odd-power classification for nonabelian groups is established here.
